validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real, actively tracked infrastructure. PNGRB's NGPL register (line-wise common-carrier authorisation list, PL Unique ID 5.08.NGPL) carries 'Ennore-Tuticorin', entity IOCL, authorised 10.12.2015, authorised length 1,431 km, authorised capacity 84.67 MMSCMD -- exact match to the sheet's LengthKnown/Capacity -- continuously from the earliest archived edition (as-on 31.03.2021, wayback-captured NGPL-25062021.pdf) through the current live May-2026 MIS report. gem.wiki's own citation list independently names the full project as 'Ennore-Thiruvallur-Bengaluru-Puducherry-Nagapattinam-Madurai-Tuticorin natural gas pipeline' (ETBPNMTPL) per a PNGRB July-2014 bid document -- the sheet's shortened/typo'd 'Ennore-Tuticorn-Bengalaru' name is a mangled abbreviation of that same official name, not a different project. Correctly classified as a transmission trunk (PNGRB's 'Common Carrier Natural Gas Pipeline' category is definitionally transmission, not gathering/feeder). DUPLICATE: checked against the 27-pipeline roster -- no match; P0921 Ennore-Nellore is a different corridor and different authorised entity (GTIL, not IOCL), correctly a separate GEM row, not this line under another name. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1=Indian Oil Corp 100% matches the register's 'IOCL' entity for this exact PL Unique ID; StartLocation=Ennore/EndLocation=Tuticorin (both Tamil Nadu) match, and the register's 'passing through' states (TN, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Puducherry) are consistent with the full corridor name transiting Bengaluru/Puducherry/Nagapattinam/Madurai as waypoints (GEM's schema only records start/end state, which is fine). See separate SPEC concern below on StartYear1.

validity.recommendation: Correct StartYear1 from 2025 to ~2021 (evidence-backed; exact month uncertain). Also consider whether this line should be modelled as a phased operating+construction pair (like P0938/P3602 Mallavaram-Bhopal) rather than one row wholly at 'construction', since the register shows the large majority already commercially operating.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's StartYear1=2025 is contradicted by PNGRB's own multi-year NGPL register history for this exact line (PL Unique ID 5.08.NGPL, entity IOCL, 1,431 km / 84.67 MMSCMD -- unchanged identifiers throughout, so this is unambiguously the same authorisation being tracked over time): as-on 31.03.2021 (captured in NGPL-25062021.pdf), the register already lists 165.82 km OPERATING / 1,265.18 km under construction, with the 165.82 km segment's own target date ('Feb, 2021') already met. That 165.82/1,265.18 split is IDENTICAL across the Sep-2021, Dec-2021, 31.03.2022 ('Partially Commissioned Common Carrier Natural Gas Pipelines' table) and May-2022 editions -- a full year of zero further progress despite a slipping target (Feb 2022 -> June 2022). By 31.12.2022 operating length had grown to 281.80 km; by the Feb/June-2024 editions it had jumped to 1,080 km (75%); by March-2025 to 1,087 km; June-2025 to 1,094 km; and the current May-2026 report shows 1,121 of 1,431 km (78.3%) operating, gas already flowing at 5.9 MMSCMD, with 310 km still under construction and the target completion date ('Mar-25' per the current report) already lapsed. So first commercial gas on this corridor happened by early 2021 at the latest -- roughly four years before the sheet's recorded StartYear1=2025 -- and construction has proceeded in slow, repeatedly-delayed phases since (Trap #3: sectional commissioning, not one event), consistent with the PNGRB register being the origin of Capacity/Length on this row (per country guidance, citing it is correct but not independent corroboration for those two fields) while remaining independent, primary evidence that the recorded START date is wrong. NOTE ON VERIFICATION: url_verifier's automated substring check FAILs on both PDFs cited here because they are large multi-page scans/reports and the extractor does not reach the relevant page (page 5 of 15 in the May-2026 report; page 15-16 of 16 in the 2021 report) -- this is the documented 'large PDF' limitation in url_verifier.py's own header comments. Both URLs return live 200s, and I independently confirmed the exact matching rows via direct PyPDF2 text extraction (page-anchored, quoted in this note), which is the prescribed workaround.

Single-origin, tier medium.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status=construction is still technically accurate: PNGRB's May-2026 NGPL register (line 5.08.NGPL, 'partially commissioned' section) shows 1,121 of 1,431 km (78.3%) operating and flowing 5.9 MMSCMD, but a genuine 310 km remains under construction with the target completion date ('Mar-25') already lapsed -- so this is not a stale/dormant authorisation (Trap #4 does not apply; there is real, if slow, ongoing build-out and active gas flow), just a slow multi-year build whose target keeps slipping (Feb 2021 -> June 2022 -> March 2024 -> March 2025 -> still open May 2026). Flagging for the record: the single-row model (one row, one Status, covering the full 1,431 km) understates how much is already commercially operating -- GEM models an analogous case (Mallavaram-Bhopal-Bhilwara-Vijaipur) as a phased operating/construction pair (P0938/P3602); this line has no such companion row. Not proposing a Status change here (construction remains the accurate description of the whole corridor's completion state), but see the linked validity SPEC flag: StartYear1=2025 is wrong given the register already shows 165.82 km operating as of the 31.03.2021 edition -- should read ~2021, not 2025.

summary: P0922 (Ennore-Tuticorin) is a real IOCL common-carrier trunk, correctly classified, no duplicate, no ownership error, Length/Capacity/Owner filled with PNGRB register refs; StartYear1=2025 is a genuine SPEC error (register shows 165.82 km already operating by the 31.03.2021 edition, now 1,121/1,431 km by May 2026) -- should read ~2021; Status=construction confirmed as still accurate given 310 km genuinely remains unbuilt; SegmentCost left UNRESOLVED.
